title.rendered: Over P200-B in investments promises more jobs for ASEAN member states

content.rendered:
By Dean Aubrey Caratiquet

Amid the backdrop of global uncertainty, Southeast Asian countries continue to benefit from a steady stream of foreign investments on future jobs and projects.

This, as the Association of Southeast Asian Nations’ (ASEAN) 11 member states recorded USD 243.9 billion in investments in 2025—representing the fifth consecutive year where investments exceeded USD 200 billion.

Trade and Industry Undersecretary Ceferino Rodolfo said in a statement on Saturday, “The message from ASEAN today is clear: ASEAN remains open for business, committed to regional cooperation, and determined to compete successfully in the industries of the future.”

That confidence is already turning into jobs Filipinos can point to. Projects the Philippines approved in 2025 alone are projected to create more than 153,000 jobs, and projects approved in just the first six months of 2026 add nearly 54,000 more, over 200,000 jobs already in the pipeline in a year and a half of approvals. 

Separately, the government’s Green Lane program, which fast-tracks the country’s biggest strategic investments, has certified 239 projects worth P6.32 trillion since it started. Once those are fully built and running, they’re expected to employ around 421,000 people.

Beyond increasing volumes of investment unhampered by recent developments unhampered by trade tensions, Usec. Rodolfo underscored the importance of using these investments to generate innovation, create additional jobs, and foster sustainable development.

Meanwhile, 11 companies will be honored on Tuesday at the Ninth ASEAN Inclusive Business Forum in Pasay City in recognition of their efforts towards incorporating people usually left out of the formal economy into profitable ventures that contribute to their respective economies.

These include the following, to name a few:

  • Coffee chain Foreword Coffee (Singapore)
  • Agri-food company Confirel (Cambodia)
  • Spice enterprise Agradaya (Indonesia)
  • Natural and herbal products company M2T (Timor-Leste)
  • Kawayan Collective (Philippines)

The forum forms part of the series of meetings ahead of the 49th ASEAN Summit that will be held in November.

title.rendered: NCRPO on full alert, deploys over 15K personnel for Sept. 21 rally

content.rendered:
By Christopher Lloyd Caliwan | Philippine News Agency

The National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) will be placed on full alert starting Sept. 19 to ensure peace and security ahead of rallies scheduled for Sept. 21 in Metro Manila, the Philippine National Police (PNP) said on Thursday.

The full alert status will start at 12 midnight Friday, and full deployment will be done by Saturday afternoon, PNP Spokesperson PCol. Allen Rae Co told reporters in a press briefing in Camp Crame.

The full alert status is the PNP’s highest operational readiness and security deployment, suspending all leaves for officers and requiring all personnel of the units concerned to be on standby.

“So we will be deploying more than 15,700 personnel, and the instruction is that all security personnel will not be carrying their firearms. Our body-worn cameras will be used for the said security operations,” said PCol. Co.

However, he did not specify when the full alert status would be lifted.

The PNP is particularly concerned about the incident that happened on the same date last year wherein a small youth group burned vehicles and attacked police personnel on the roads leading to Malacañang Palace.

Police investigation later revealed that there was a plan to attack Malacañang at that time.

PCol. Co said security will be in place on all the roads leading to Malacañang to foil a similar attempt this year.

“We have contingency plans in place. We do not see any specific threats as of now but we are continuously monitoring the situation. If we receive information, we would verify, validate and act if we need to,” said PCol. Co.

The official, however, asked the protesters to police their own rank and help prevent confrontation with the police.

“The PNP respects everyone’s rights to peacefully assemble but what we want to remind the people is that their constitutional protection ends when another person’s rights are violated,” PCol. Co said.

“All CDM (civil disturbance management) personnel will not be carrying their firearms. Our body-worn cameras will be used for the said security operations,” he maintained.

He added that the chief PNP has given a directive to exercise maximum tolerance at all times and all instances during the protests.

Co further noted that the police force has yet to monitor any security threats.

Security deployment not “overkill”

He also reminded protesters to observe ordinances banning the burning of effigies and the wearing of balaclavas and face coverings in public establishments and while dismounted from motorcycles in the City of Manila.

Co disputed the “overkill” tag, asserting that PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. had directed the agency to exercise “maximum tolerance” for the anticipated protests.

“’Di bale nang medyo sumobra na sinasabi nila, pero ma-ensure naman natin na yung general public will not be endangered and will not be inconvenienced,” he said.

“Ginawan ito ng pag-aaral. Ginawan ito ng pag-uusap kasama yung ating stakeholders na concerned dito sa activity na ito. Dito nakita yung pangangailangan para masiguro natin ang kaayusan sa araw na iyon,” he added.

NCRPO Officer-in-charge PBGen. Christopher Abrahano said the regional police force will be raising its alert level for the protest-actions.

“Kailangan natin ng maraming tao. Wala munang leave. Kailangan tulong-tulong muna at we need a pool of policemen para magbantay sa mga kalsada natin. Ang desire ng ating pamunuan ni chief PNP na tulong-tulong yung mga kalapit regions to ensure the capital is safe,” he said.

“We are also establishing coordination with the known leaders of these groups to warn them, to make arrangements with them this early,” Abrahano added.

On Sept. 21, 2025, anti-corruption rallies were held in parts of the NCR, stemming from public outrage over the flood control and infrastructure corruption scandal.

title.rendered: DTI: Essential Noche Buena items remain at 2023 prices

content.rendered:
By Anna Leah Gonzales | Philippine News Agency

The Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) has released the 2024 Noche Buena products price guide, noting many of these essential items have remained at their 2023 prices while others have even decreased.

In a statement on Sunday, the DTI said the guide includes prices for 236 stock keeping units (SKUs) from 22 Noche Buena manufacturers across 12 categories: ham, queso de bola, fruit cocktail, cheese, sandwich spread, all-purpose cream, mayonnaise, pasta noodles, elbow and salad macaroni, and tomato and spaghetti sauce. 

The DTI said the price stability is reflected in 121 SKUs, including holiday staples such as certain brands of ham, fruit cocktail, queso de bola, sandwich spread, cheese, spaghetti sauce, tomato sauce, and all-purpose cream.

The 13 SKUs with price reductions include select brands of mayonnaise, pasta, elbow macaroni, salad macaroni, and all-purpose cream.

The DTI said the price guide aims to provide consumers with a broad selection of options this holiday season. 

The prices of ham ranges from P170 to P928.50; queso de bola, from P210 to P445; fruit cocktail, from P61.76 to P302.50; cheese, from P56.50 to P310; mayonnaise, from P20.40 to P245.85; and all-purpose cream, from P36.50 to PHP72. 

Prices of sandwich spread, meanwhile, ranges from P27 to P263.60; pasta or spaghetti, from P32 to P114; elbow macaroni, from P30.50 to P126.25; tomato sauce, from P16.50 to P92.85; salad macaroni, from P36.50 to P126.25, and spaghetti sauce, from P28.50 to P103.

The prices listed in the Noche Buena price guide will remain effective until Dec. 31 to ensure access to reasonably priced products through Media Noche. 

“Aligned with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s directive to promote consumer rights and responsibilities, this year’s Noche Buena Price Guide demonstrates the DTI’s commitment to empowering Filipino families to make informed choices,” DTI Acting Secretary Cristina Roque said. 

“By publishing this price guide, the DTI urges consumers to compare prices and select products that best fit their budget and preferences for the holiday season.” 

The DTI advised consumers to check expiration dates to ensure product quality and consider bulk purchases for potential cost savings per unit. 

Additional special promotions and discounts may be available, offering further opportunities to save. 

The complete details of the 2024 Noche Buena price guide is uploaded in the DTI website and social media platforms. 

The DTI said it would closely monitor Noche Buena item prices nationwide.  

If items are priced above the guide, consumers may report them to the 1-DTI hotline (1-384) or email consumercare@dti.gov.ph.

By Gabriela Baron

The National Museum of the Philippines declared Malate Church as an important cultural property in the country, the city government of Manila announced over the weekend.

This is is accordance with the Presidential Decree No. 374 and the Republic Act. No. 10066 or the National Cultural Heritage Act.

The Our Lady of Remedies Parish, a 435-year old Mexican-Baroque styled church in Malate, Manila, was considered a qualifier under the category of Spanish colonial era church.

Important cultural properties may receive subsidies and other supporting measures from the government for its preservation and conservation.

These establishments are defined as cultural properties possessing “exceptional cultural, artistic, and/or historical significance.”

It is the second level of protection after the classification of National Cultural Treasures.

These properties may be declared by the National Commission for Culture and Arts, National Historical Commission of the Philippines, and the National Museum of the Philippines.

title.rendered: 2 drug suspects slain in Sultan Kudarat shootout

content.rendered:
KIDAPAWAN CITY – Two suspected drug personalities were killed in a shootout with authorities while another one managed to escape a law enforcement operation in Columbio, Sultan Kudarat Monday evening, police said.

Supt. Aldrin Gonzales, Police Regional Office 12 (PRO-12) spokesperson, said that a report by the Columbio police to PRO-12 Director Chief Supt. Eliseo Rasco identified the slain suspects as Nonoy Sangkala, 25; and Leslie Barrientos Lampig, 45, both of Barangay Tambak, Lambayong, Sultan Kudarat.

Another suspect, identified as Boy Makalanga, 45, of Columbio, Sultan Kudarat, managed to elude arrest. Gonzales said joint operatives of the Regional Prohibited Drug Enforcement Unit (RPDEU-12) and the Columbio municipal police office conducted the buy-bust operation at 9:45 p.m.

The suspects later sensed they were dealing with a poseur-buyer and fled but firing their guns toward law enforcement officers, triggering a brief gun battle.

Two of the three suspects were initially injured and rushed by the police to a hospital, where they were declared dead on arrival.

Seized from the slain suspects were a huge sachet of shabu, PHP1,000 drug buy-bust money, an Ingram submachine pistol and a .38 caliber revolver.

Gonzales said all three suspects were included on the RPDEU-12 drug watch list. (Edwin Fernandez/PNA)
